paper_summary: Russian-language VIAM paper (Chursova, Sokolov, Lukina, 2017) describing two new lightweight core materials for aircraft sandwich structures: a closed-cell syntactic foam (spheroplastic) grade VPZ-17 made from a high-deformability cyanate-ester binder (VST-1210, an aryl dicyanate oligomer plus cycloaliphatic epoxy) filled with hollow glass microspheres (grades MS-VP / MS-VP-A9), and a chemically blown phenolic-rubber foam grade VPP-4 (not a hollow-particle composite). The syntactic foam is produced by blending binder with microspheres, calendering into <=2 mm sheets, cutting and molding plates; it has a density of 0.67 g/cm3 and retains useful strength up to 160-180 C. Reported spheroplastic values: 33/31 MPa tensile, 92/63 MPa compressive and 80/54 MPa flexural strength at 20/160 C.

extraction_notes: Paper is in Russian; 'сферопластик' (spheroplastic) = syntactic foam. Six records extracted from Table 1 (grade VPZ-17), one per test type x test temperature (20 C and 160 C). Only strengths and bulk density are reported; no moduli, strains, volume/weight fractions, particle size or particle density are given anywhere in the paper, so those fields are null. Density 0.67 g/cm3 is listed only in the 20 C column and was carried over to the 160 C records as the material's density. The Charpy impact toughness (5,5 kJ/m2 at 20 C, GOST 4647-49) and the dielectric permittivity data (2.07 as-received, 2.27 after 30 days at 98% RH, 2.13 after 1 day drying, at 10^10 Hz) have no matching schema fields and were therefore not turned into records. Table 2 reports properties of sandwich panels (glass- or carbon-fibre skins over the spheroplastic core: densities 1.2 and 1.0 g/cm3; tensile 250/220 and 340/360 MPa; compressive 315/270 and 323/238 MPa; flexural 531/507 and 697/483 MPa at 20/160 C) - these are multilayer structures, not the hollow-particle composite itself, so they were excluded. Table 3 (phenolic foams FK-20 and VPP-4, densities 190-230 and 80-150 kg/m3) describes chemically blown closed-cell foams with no hollow particles and was excluded as out of scope. Process route recorded as compression_molding: binder + microspheres were mixed, calendered into sheets <=2 mm, cut and then molded into plates; no cure temperature was given for the spheroplastic.
